newsitem.title: GERMANY: NordLB expects sustained growth in H2 1997.
newsitem.headline: NordLB expects sustained growth in H2 1997.

text.p: The German regional bank Norddeutsche Landesbank said on Thursday that group net earnings before risk provisions rose 6.4 percent to 448.3 million marks in the first half of 1997.
NordLB said it expected sustained levels of growth in the second half of the year.
The group said net commissions received were 145.2 million marks, a rise of 14.7 percent, while interest earnings were 896.1 million marks, up 6.4 percent.
NordLB's balance sheet total was 247.3 billion marks, up 7.7 percent. Growth was driven by the group's credit business, its interbank business and the expansion of its debt holdings.
The increase in net commissions came primarily from the dynamic development of the group's securities business.

In full-year 1996, NordLB reported earnings after provisions of 366.9 million marks, down from 450.8 million marks the previous year. The balance sheet total was 229.6 billion marks, up from 208.9 billion marks.
